products.title: Monthly Economic Update — August 2026
products.description: The monthly update between quarterly editions, data to July 2026, covering everything since the July quarterly update of 3 August. Gateshead's claimant count for July 2026 is 5,035 people, 4.0% of residents aged 16-64 — 45 higher than June but only 10 higher than July 2025, flat on the year at +0.2% while the North East rose 2.0% and England 1.1%. A year earlier the borough was falling in step with the region (−12.5% against −12.8%); it has now come off the regional path, and for once on the better side. The 18-24 claimant count is 990, up 8.8% since June 2025. Ward detail shows Felling at 6.6% against Low Fell at 1.4%, with Saltwell up 50 claimants since January. The 2024 household income year landed on 19 August: gross disposable household income per head is £19,745, up 5.8% nominal, against £25,965 for the UK and £20,562 for the North East — 338th of 361 UK local authorities, and an index against the UK of 76.0, the lowest since 2008 and a third consecutive annual fall. Real household income per head grew 2.2% in the North East, the weakest of the twelve ITL1 regions. No new Annual Population Survey quarter this month, so the survey measures are shown at their true period with their confidence intervals and marked as carrying no new data; the payrolled employee figure is left blank until its quarterly refresh on 15 September.
products.sources: NOMIS (Claimant Count NM_162_1, incl. 2024 wards; Annual Population Survey NM_17_5) — ONS Regional GDHI 1997 to 2024, released 19 August 2026 — ONS Labour market overview August 2026 — ONS Consumer price inflation July 2026 — MHCLG Housing Delivery Test 2024 and 2025 measurements

products.title: What's New — 25 August 2026
products.description: Covering 17 to 25 August — a nine-day window, because the Monday edition ran a day late and the rule is to cover every day since the last one. Three genuinely local numbers landed. Gateshead's gross disposable household income per head for 2024 is £19,745, up 5.8% on 2023, against £25,965 for the UK and £20,562 for the North East; the borough ranks 338th of 361 UK local authorities and its index against the UK slipped again, 77.5 in 2019 to 76.3 in 2023 to 76.0 in 2024. The Housing Delivery Test 2025 measurement puts Gateshead at 105% with no consequence, up from 93% and an action plan on the 2024 measurement, on the strength of 546 net additions in 2024/25; Newcastle falls to 87%, North and South Tyneside stay under the presumption. The July claimant count is 5,035 (4.0% of residents aged 16-64), flat on the year at +0.2% against +2.0% for the North East and +1.1% for England, with the 18-24 count up 8.8%. On policy: England has a new National Planning Policy Framework, published 17 August with two consultation responses and a rules-based policy statement, which reached us five days late; the Department for Business and Trade has been renamed the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade; and the non-fiscal half of the 31 July Cabinet Statement Rewiring the State is reported here for the first time, including the commitment to align police forces, fire and rescue services and Integrated Care Boards to strategic authority boundaries. Carries the complete departmental log — 53 items, reconciled against the mailroom digest.
products.sources: Weekly round-up — ONS — NOMIS — gov.uk — ONS release calendar — team mailbox

products.title: What's New — 17 August 2026
products.description: Covering 10 to 17 August. No local statistics landed, but the statistical status of the survey behind every Gateshead employment figure was settled. On 11 August the ONS confirmed to the regulator that Labour Force Survey and Annual Population Survey outputs move from official statistics in development to official statistics, and that it will not seek reaccreditation for them — regional GDHI excepted. The same letter names reductions in the APS sample boost, with quality advice due alongside the September dataset. The first Transformed Labour Force Survey readiness assessment concluded now is not the right time to transition; the LFS remains the lead source, with a decision point in July 2027 and transition planned for November 2027. Separately, a national high street package would require planning permission for vape shops and adult gaming centres, revoke the Gambling Act aim to permit duty and double closure orders to 12 months — four weeks before the high streets inquiry closes to evidence on 7 September. Three corrections to our own record: GDHI is confirmed for 19 August after losing its date, the productivity method paper is 28 September rather than November, and UK Business Counts is 24 September rather than the autumn. New local authority breakdowns in the Community and Engagement Survey are the only genuinely new local data.
products.sources: Weekly round-up · ONS release calendar · NOMIS · gov.uk · parliament.uk · team mailbox

products.title: Policy Update — August 2026
products.description: What changed in government and regional policy for Gateshead's economy — third edition, scan run 10 August 2026 covering 13 July to 10 August. Four weeks that changed the framework: mayors get a share of business rates from April 2027 and of income tax from 2028, explicitly replacing central grant, with the equalisation design still undefined and the detail due at the Budget on 28 October. Local growth and devolution policy left MHCLG and the Treasury for No10 North in Manchester on 23 July. A 20% business rates discount for pubs, social clubs and live music venues from April 2027 lands on premises in the priority local centres the team holds no baseline for. VAT comes off domestic electricity on 1 October and the £2 bus fare cap returns in January 2027. The high streets select committee inquiry closes to written evidence on 7 September. Plus: the Transformed Labour Force Survey readiness assessment, quarterly regional GDP returning at ITL1 only, and a component-based rebuild of the headline productivity statistic timed for the same month as our 2024 local figure.
products.sources: Briefing · HTML · gov.uk · parliament.uk · ONS · NE MSA

products.title: What's New — 10 August 2026
products.description: Covering 3 to 10 August. No local statistics landed, but a date we were relying on came off the calendar and the machinery behind two core measures is being changed in the open. Regional gross disposable household income, 1997 to 2024 no longer carries a confirmed day — the ONS release page now reads provisional August 2026, where last week it read 19 August. The ONS improvement plan confirms an August readiness assessment for moving to the Transformed Labour Force Survey as the headline labour market measure in 2027, and names a new component-based method for the headline productivity statistic, timed for November alongside the 5 November subregional productivity release. Also: the Employment Rights Act timeline (electronic and workplace balloting from 25 August), reissued Youth Jobs Grant guidance, quarterly public service productivity and UK R&D spend for 2024 with no regional breakdown. The high streets inquiry closes to written evidence on 7 September.
products.sources: Weekly round-up · ONS release calendar · NOMIS · gov.uk · parliament.uk · team mailbox

products.title: What's New — 3 August 2026
products.description: Covering 28 July to 3 August. Two releases that change what we can measure and one date that fixes the autumn. New mid-2025 population estimates (29 Jul) reset the denominator under every per-head rate we publish. Workless households 2025 carries local authority tables, giving us the only LA-level measure of children in workless households. The Budget is confirmed for Wednesday 28 October, which is when the fiscal devolution roadmap and devolution white paper land and the mechanism behind mayoral income tax and business rates retention finally becomes visible. Also: DWP's first Get Britain Working labour market insights, MHCLG council tax and business rates collection rates at billing authority level, and MSOA health state life expectancy. Autumn dates now firm for GDHI (19 Aug), UK Business Counts (24 Sep) and subregional productivity (5 Nov); GVA 2024 remains provisional for September 2026 with no day confirmed.
products.sources: Weekly round-up · ONS release calendar · NOMIS · gov.uk · team mailbox

products.title: Quarterly Economic Update — July 2026
products.description: The quarterly economic update, data to June 2026. Both administrative series softened over the quarter. The claimant count rose 60 to 5,090 in June 2026 (4.0% of residents aged 16-64) and payrolled employees fell 405 to 86,312 in May 2026, though over the year both are lower. The payroll fall of 0.4% sits alongside 0.4% for the North East and 0.3% for England, and those gaps are smaller than the revisions the source makes between consecutive editions, so no ranking should be read into them. None of the four headline Annual Population Survey measures moved far enough to clear its own confidence interval, on the quarter or the year, and Gateshead is not statistically distinguishable from the North East or England on any of them. Gateshead has been above the North East on the claimant proportion in every one of the last fifteen months and within two tenths of a point of England throughout. House prices are up 6.3% on the year against England 2.3%. Real regular pay growth has narrowed to about a third of a point, from 1.2 points a year ago. Includes the standing indicator table with confidence intervals on every survey estimate.
products.sources: NOMIS (Claimant Count NM_162_1, Annual Population Survey NM_17_5) - ONS and HMRC PAYE RTI (June and July 2026 editions) - HM Land Registry UK HPI - ONS consumer prices, national accounts, vacancies, producer prices and BICS

products.title: What's New — 28 July 2026
products.description: The Monday 27 July edition, covering 20–28 July. The month's biggest data drop landed on 21 July — claimant count to June 2026 and a new Annual Population Survey window (Apr 2025–Mar 2026) that the Quarterly Economy Monitor must be built on. MHCLG's local-authority business rates and reliefs data is the easy-to-miss one. Policy: local economic growth policy moved out of MHCLG and HM Treasury to No.10 North on 22 July, DSIT abolished, and a 14+ technical education announcement aimed at NEETs — an intention, not yet policy. Two deadlines close Friday 31 July: the Northern Growth Strategy views window and the Productivity Institute call for papers.
products.sources: Weekly round-up · ONS release calendar · NOMIS · gov.uk · team mailbox

products.title: What's New — 20 July 2026
products.description: First full edition of the weekly round-up. A big data week ahead: UK Labour Market with local claimant count and PAYE RTI (21 Jul), June CPI (22 Jul), and the confirmed mid-2025 population estimates with revised back series (29 Jul) — all feeding the 30 Jul Quarterly Economy Monitor. Policy: the Commons HCLG Committee's Revitalising High Streets inquiry (evidence closes 7 Sep), a change of Prime Minister, and Skills England's move to DWP. Live deadline: Northern Growth Strategy views close 31 July.

products.title: Policy Update — July 2026
products.description: What changed in government and regional policy for Gateshead's economy — second edition, scan run 13 July 2026: the Northern Growth Strategy views window closing 31 July (£120m, proposed Newcastle–Gateshead MDZ), Gateshead named a North East Pathfinder partner, the new North East LSIP 2026–2029, the Industrial Strategy quarterly and year-one reports (8 July), the April 2026 Universal Credit structural break, and the Transformed LFS transition timetable under assessment. products.title: Local Outcomes Framework comparator
products.description: Where Gateshead sits on MHCLG's Local Outcomes Framework (first edition, 1 July 2026) across all 16 outcomes, against six switchable comparator groups — MHCLG's statistical neighbours, NECA 7, the North East 12, the ONS economic neighbours, and the national median with and without London. MHCLG publishes no dataset for the framework and its digital tool is not yet live, so each of the 112 live metrics is assembled from the original publication the framework names, across 12 publishing organisations, and rendered as 137 series (49 with published 95% confidence intervals). Group median, rank, quintile band and a better/worse reading per metric against all 132 English single-tier authorities, with a ranked comparator chart, trends, and a data-currency panel driven by the quarterly vintage sweep. A comparator tool, not an assessment of council performance: where a rank would mislead, none is given, and the 3 metrics MHCLG has not yet confirmed show as visible awaiting-data rows.
products.sources: MHCLG Local Outcomes Framework · assembled from OHID, ONS, NOMIS, DfE, DHSC/ASCOF, MHCLG, DfT, Defra, DCMS, DWP, NDTMS, Sport England, Skills for Care
